title: 2011 AMC 12A Problem 8
statement: In the eight-term sequence \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E,\) \(F,\) \(G,\) \(H,\) the value of \(C\) is \(5\) and the sum of any three consecutive terms is \(30.\) What is \(A + H?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(A + B + C = B + C + D = 30,\) we get \(D = A,\) and likewise the sequence repeats with period \(3.\) Thus \(H,\) the eighth term, equals \(B.\)

From \(A + B + C = 30\) and \(C = 5,\) we have \(A + H = A + B = 30 - 5 = 25.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Consecutive triples having equal sums forces the sequence to repeat every three terms
So \(H\) equals \(B,\) which means \(A + H\) is the same as \(A + B\)
